description: Privacy gate before logging or forwarding text: does it contain personal data that identifies a specific private individual.

contains_pii.instructions: Does the text contain personal data about a specific private individual? Treat people as real unless the text frames them as an example or placeholder. Counts: a phone number, personal email, street address, national ID, card or account number, or health data tied to a person, with or without a name. Does not count: company or role mailboxes, public figures in their public role, opaque internal user ids, and partial card numbers (last four digits).

criteria.true: Contains personal data of a real private individual
criteria.false: No personal data of a private individual

cases.state: Incident summary, payments service, 6 October. Between 14:02 and 14:47 UTC about 3% of card authorizations failed with a timeout from the acquirer. The on-call engineer was paged at 14:05 through the payments-oncall rotation and opened a bridge at 14:09. Initial suspicion was our own connection pool, but pool metrics were normal. At 14:31 the acquirer's status page confirmed degraded performance in their EU region. We enabled failover to the secondary acquirer at 14:40 and error rates returned to baseline by 14:47. Affected requests were retried automatically; a sample of affected sessions includes user ids u_44120, u_90813 and u_12077, and the failed authorizations were for cards ending 1881, 0423 and 7740. No customer was charged twice. Follow-ups: lower the failover threshold from 10% to 3% errors, add an alert on acquirer latency, and ask the acquirer for a written root cause within two weeks, and review the runbook at the next team meeting. Questions about this report can go to payments-team@acme-corp.com.
cases.rationale: Only opaque user ids, last-four card digits and a team mailbox.
